title: Reconcile credit assignment after meter pulse reordering causing invoice drift
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers reported mid-cycle invoice deltas where rate-limit credits and partial-hour credits were applied to neighboring invoice lines, causing net invoice amounts to shift by a few cents to dollars. Root cause appears to be out-of-order 'meter pulses' (sub-minute metering events) when ingestion retries and leader-election reorder events occurred, which then mismatches the original usage window that should receive the credit. This ticket scopes detection, reconciliation, and a safe corrective export for Stripe/NetSuite that preserves idempotency and auditability.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate high-retry scenario for a tenant with sub-minute spikes and rate-limit throttling. 2) Inject out-of-order metering events with synthetic timestamps (t, t-20s, t+10s) and ensure ingestion race occurs. 3) Run current export pipeline to generate Stripe line items and NetSuite reconciler output. 4) Observe credit lines attached to the wrong hour bucket and invoice summary mismatch with expected per-hour apportionment.
investigation: Initial logs show ingestion sequencer occasionally emitted pulses with non-monotonic sequence numbers when a host crashed during leader-hand off. The export worker groups events by hour-window anchored to receive timestamp instead of original usage_timestamp, which introduced drift. We found the reconciler lacks deterministic tie-breaker when sequences are near the hour boundary. Analysis of 30 impacted invoices shows a common pattern: a credit line moved to the previous hour when a retry arrived late but was backdated in the original usage timestamp.
proposed_solution: 1) Change export worker to anchor grouping to canonical usage_timestamp order, using (usage_timestamp, sequence_id) as the deterministic key. 2) Add a grace-window policy for late-arriving pulses: if a pulse with earlier usage_timestamp arrives within 10 minutes, reassign but mark export as 'adjustment' rather than new line to preserve idempotency. 3) Emit an export manifest with seqnums and tombstone markers for replaced credit lines so NetSuite reconciler can apply a net-zero adjustment. 4) Add unit tests and shadow-run for 48 hours before cutover.
implementation_notes: - Update export-grouper service: switch primary sort to usage_timestamp, secondary to ingestion_seq. - Add manifest field export_seq and replaced_line_ids. - Implement idempotent replace semantics in stripe-exporter: create adjustment lines with negative/positive pairing and preserve original invoice_line_id in metadata. - Update Netsuite exporter to apply replacements via existing adjustment flow; include new checksum to detect partial application.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for ordering logic with randomized sequences. - Integration test that runs full export against a shadow Stripe sandbox and a CSV NetSuite emulator to validate net-zero adjustments. - Run production shadow export for a subset of tenants (10% sample) for 48 hours and compare diffs. - Manual spot-check on 20 affected invoices from historical incidents to verify reconstructions match expected amounts.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PR and run canary in staging. 2) Deploy export-grouper and stripe-exporter behind feature flag (reconcile-ordered-exports). 3) Enable flag for 10% of tenants, monitor invoice delta metrics and export errors for 72 hours. 4) If stable, ramp to 100% and enable NetSuite reconciler adjustments the following maintenance window.
rollback_plan: If we see >0.5% unexpected invoice delta or >3 SLO violations in exporter, flip feature flag off to revert to current exporter and run a compensating job to re-emit original manifests for any partially-applied replacements.
